newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn coalition wraps up tax reform talks.
newsitem.headline: Bonn coalition wraps up tax reform talks.

text.p: Germany's coalition tax commission has completed its work on a major tax reform programme after a marathon final meeting on Wednesday, Finance Minister Theo Waigel said.

Waigel told reporters the reform package would relieve the burden on German taxpayers by a total 70 billion marks ($42.64 billion). Taking into account the scrapping of a range of tax breaks, the net lightening of the tax load would be 30 billion marks, he said.
"This is the biggest tax reform in the history of the German Federal Republic," Waigel told reporters.
Hermann Otto Solms, chief tax negotiator for junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP), also declared himself satisfied with the result.

The key element of the package is a cut in income taxes from 1999, with a new 15 percent tax band being introduced on income from 13,000 to 20,000 marks. Tax rates would then rise on a sliding scale from 22 percent to 39 percent. The old entry rate was 26 percent, and the top rate was 53 percent.

The meeting of the tax working group was the last after months of wrangling within Chancellor Helmut Kohl's three-party coalition government. Party leaders will review the package on Thursday before Waigel announces it in full (eds: 1700 GMT). ($1=1.6415 Mark)
